evidence.claim: The Marzetti Company says its foodservice business supplies many top US restaurant chains with dressings, sauces, breads, and frozen pastas; it also lists licensed retail sauce/dressing agreements with restaurant brands including Chick-fil-A, Buffalo Wild Wings, Arby's, Subway, Olive Garden, and Texas Roadhouse.

McCormick's Flavor Solutions segment supplies foodservice customers with customized flavor solutions including seasoning blends, spices and herbs, condiments, coating systems, and compound flavors, and the filing notes long-standing customer relationships.
Sensient discloses a Flavors & Extracts Group with 2024 revenue of $793.7 million and identifies business areas including savory, sweet, beverage, BioNutrients, and natural ingredients.

Sensient may be a second-order restaurant sauce/seasoning beneficiary if its savory flavor and food/beverage systems are used by foodservice manufacturers or restaurant-chain suppliers; direct restaurant-chain exposure still needs verification.

B&G Foods' filings list products including cooking oils, spices, seasonings, hot sauces, salad dressings, Mexican-style sauces, salsas, pickles, peppers, and a Spices & Flavor Solutions segment, and state that it competes in foodservice and private-label channels among others.
evidence.source_title: B&G Foods Form 10-Q for quarter ended June 28, 2025

evidence.claim: Ventura Foods, a private company, is described as a $3 billion supplier of oils, sauces, dressings, condiments, mayonnaise, margarine, butter blends, dry seasonings, and mixes to top restaurant chains and distributors; this supports the node's private-supplier benchmark and hidden-supplier thesis.
evidence.source_title: Ventura Foods Dials up Flavor to Fuel Growth at $3 Billion Supplier - Orange County Business Journal

evidence.claim: TreeHouse Foods was acquired by Investindustrial, its common stock is no longer listed on the NYSE, and it became a private company; therefore it is a relevant private-market comp but not a current US-listed candidate.
evidence.source_title: Investindustrial Completes Acquisition of TreeHouse Foods

memory_update.text: LANC/The Marzetti Company is the cleanest US-listed direct node candidate for restaurant sauces and dressings because foodservice chain supply and licensed chain-branded sauces are explicitly disclosed.
SXT should be tracked as an upstream, underfollowed flavor-system hypothesis rather than a proven restaurant-chain sauce supplier until savory/foodservice/customer evidence is found.
BGS is a small-cap speculative-shadow candidate: node products and foodservice/private-label channel exposure are factual, but direct top-chain/custom-sauce dependency remains unproven.

TreeHouse Foods was a natural private-label foodservice screen candidate historically, but after the February 11, 2026 take-private it should move from active public universe to private comp / M&A signal bucket.

Private suppliers such as Ventura Foods validate that sauces, oils, dressings, condiments, mayonnaise, butter blends, and seasonings can be large, hidden restaurant-chain supply nodes; public screens should look beyond GICS restaurants and distributors.

node: Sauces, oils, dressings, condiments, mayonnaise, butter blends, and seasonings
summary: Layer 1B expanded the public universe around the low-visibility flavor/condiment input node. The strongest US-listed direct match is The Marzetti Company/Lancaster Colony because it explicitly supplies top US restaurant chains with dressings and sauces and sells licensed chain-branded sauces at retail. McCormick is the reference leader for custom flavor solutions, seasonings, condiments, and foodservice customer relationships. Sensient is an underfollowed ingredient-system candidate one step upstream through flavors/extracts and savory systems, but restaurant-specific sauce exposure requires verification. B&G Foods is a small-cap/speculative-shadow candidate because it owns spices, flavor solutions, hot sauces, cooking oils, salad dressings, Mexican-style sauces, and foodservice/private-label channel exposure, but the degree of top-chain/custom-manufacturing exposure is not yet proven. TreeHouse Foods was excluded from active candidates because it was taken private and delisted in February 2026.
